newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFin problem to be solved-deputy minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFin problem to be solved-deputy minister.

text.p: Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Thursday he was confident the problem of frozen MinFin bonds will be resolved once legal contradictions are sorted out.
He noted that the government had called on the judicial authorities at a meeting on November 5 to review recent freezings of MinFins.

Officials from the Finance Ministry, Interior Ministry, Central Bank, Prosecutor-General's office, Vneshekonombank (the paying agent for MinFin bonds) and Vneshtorgbank (the main depositary) attended the meeting, chaired by Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, who is in charge of economic policy.
Kasyanov said the government gave the Interior Ministry and Prosecutor-General's office a month to review all MinFin bond freezes and cancel those that were unecessarily frozen.
"Freezes will be cancelled if the Interior Ministry and Prosecutor-General's office find it poosible to do so according to the concrete laws," he said.
He said the government had also called on the judicial authorities to refrain from any sanctions against bearer bonds "unless there is a special necessity to freeze them."

They were also asked to take into account central bank recommendations on modifying current practice to avoid further freezes in the near future, before contradictions in the criminal and civil codes are eradicated, Kasyanov said.
Under criminal law, police may freeze bonds that are said to be stolen. But under civil law, bonds may not be seized from owners who acquired them in good faith.
Kasyanov said the Interior Ministry and Prosecutor-General should submit proposals to the government on eliminating legal contradictions by November 25.

"The problem is not that the issuer (the Finance Ministry) is unable to pay coupons. We paid all the money. It is a legal contradiction that does not allow the bondholders to receive the money. We hope investors understand it," Kasyanov said.
"The aim of the government, Finance Ministry and central bank is to put an end to this contradiction so that there would be no worries and concerns among investors," he added.

A Moscow district prosecutor's office issued an order to freeze $56.81 million face value in June. The bonds were frozen as part of an investigation into the head of a small bank which has since closed.

This would bring the total bonds currently known to have been frozen to $74 million, including around $24 million already detailed by the finance ministry in July, some of which had been stolen in the breakaway republic of Chechnya.
Owners of previously frozen MinFins have not received coupon payments which the Finance Ministry transferred to Vneshekonombank.
